Claire —

Appreciate the clarity. Quick answers up front: yes we can support a July go-live with the right commits; we propose a two-phase capacity plan so Horizon can start with a small dedicated pool and scale into private deployment for regulated data.

Proposed starting configuration (subject to technical POC):
- US-West (primary): 8 x A100-40GB per dedicated pool (+KV cache), expected steady-state 120 RPS for chat at 512 tokens; peak burst target 220 RPS with autoscaling to private nodes.
- US-East (secondary/DR): 4 x A100-40GB, reserved for failover and lower concurrency workloads.
- Latency estimate: 60–90ms token time (end-to-end) at 512 tokens for the A100 path when caching is effective.

Evaluation plan:
- Week 0: technical POC (2 weeks) — model parity tests, throughput/latency, KV prefix caching verification.
- Week 2–6: production trial (4 weeks) — live traffic mirror up to 30% of production, SLO tracking, cost snapshots.

I'll loop in Aditya (solutions) and Marcus (runtime) to provide exact GPU counts and a sizing workbook. Can procurement share any constraints on region residency or minimum contract terms?

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Kickoff — MAP: Dedicated/private capacity & evaluation timeline

Adding some technical constraints and throughput assumptions so the MAP has concrete acceptance criteria.

Key notes:
- Model: we assume using a 13B dense model (we suggested a quantized INT8 path if Horizon can accept slight quality regression — saves ~2.5x GPU memory and allows 2x concurrency per GPU).
- Baseline token throughput: one A100-40GB serving the 13B quantized path ~ 110–140 RPS (short responses, typical chat workload).
- For the 200 RPS peak Horizon requested: recommend 12 A100-40GB (primary) with autoscale headroom to add +4 GPUs for short bursts.
- For the conservative start (to control cost): start with 8 A100 with a MAP commitment to add GPUs by the end of week 3 of the technical POC if 95th percentile RPS > 90% of target.

Acceptance criteria for technical POC:
- 95th pctl latency at 512 tokens under 250ms
- Throughput: sustain 150 RPS for a 10-minute window without queuing
- KV prefix cache hit-rate >= 35% for our prompt set

Link to evaluation-plan outline: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-eval-plan (internal doc).

- Aditya
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Kickoff — MAP: Dedicated/private capacity & evaluation timeline

Folks —

Attached is an initial sizing workbook (gpu_sizing_sheet_q2.xlsx) with regional breakdowns and throughput projections. Summary pasted below for quick visibility:

Regional sizing (initial commit):
- US-West (primary): 8 x A100-40GB dedicated; expected baseline throughput 110 RPS, with warm autoscale policy to +4 GPUs for short bursts up to 220 RPS.
- US-East (secondary): 4 x A100-40GB reserved for DR and nightly batch jobs (50–70 RPS).
- Observability and tracing: extra 1 x T4 per region for monitoring agents and lightweight reranking workloads.

Cost/commit options:
- Monthly reserved pool (preferred): 12 GPUs committed across regions (discount tier B).
- Short-term (POC-only): 8 GPUs in US-West + burst pool on-demand (higher unit cost).

Notes on latency and KV caching:
- With prefix caching tuned (Aditya will provide sample prompts) the effective token runtime for interactive flows is in the 45–85ms range per token; contiguous 512-token responses average ~200–220ms end-to-end.

I'll flag two engineering risks that affect the MAP timeline:
1) Model quantization parity checks — need 3 business days to run quality regressions across the eval set.
2) Networking path for private deployment (Horizon VPC peering) — networking team needs a completed network diagram and firewall rules before we can finalize private nodes provisioning (we estimate 5 business days after network approval).

Marcus Lin
Runtime Product Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com

- Infra requests that US-East carry at least 25% of baseline capacity for regional failover testing during the trial.

—Claire
